taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it was formerly treated as conspecific with the great-tailed grackle (Q. mexicanus) and is often placed in genus Cassidix.
fieldMarks: Male 38-50 cm with a long, rounded, wedge-shaped tail; entirely dark
Female much smaller (27-34 cm) than the male
Iris yellow from northeast Florida north; dark on the Texas-Louisiana coast (young great-tailed grackles also have dark eyes)
Call is a harsh repeated 'jeeb', unlike the whistles and clucks of the great-tailed grackle
behavior: Forages by walking on shore or in shallow water and steals food from larger birds
Nests in noisy colonies near water; males display with wing-fluttering and harsh calls
habitat: Marshes, beaches and coastal areas, almost always near water; inland only in Florida, generally near marshes and lakes.
range: Coastal eastern US from Long Island and New Jersey south through peninsular Florida and west along the Gulf coast to southeastern Texas; absent from the western Florida Panhandle. Not a Canadian species.

lookalikes.name: Great-tailed grackle
lookalikes.howToTell: Slightly longer-tailed and less round-headed; whistles and clucks rather than harsh jeebs.

lookalikes.name: Common grackle
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon points to it for identification in areas north of northeast Florida where boat-tailed has yellow eyes.
